note: Key written from the waverunner-website source files named in each ref, not from any skill or from memory. Shape follows evals/2026-11-24/panel.json with the brief's field names (key_points, wrong_if, working, key_source). 'scope: extension' questions need the optional fraud-report and fee extensions.

types.scheme: card-network or scheme fact as the site states it
types.provider: a named provider's rule or a secondary source as the site states it
types.site-advice: the guide's own advice, not a scheme rule

questions.question: Is there one chargeback percentage that gets a shop's payment account shut down? Everyone on the forums says 1%.

key_points.text: No chargeback ratio is a universal shutdown line.
Shopify can decline, deactivate or restrict an account before any network threshold, so a low ratio does not rule out action.
Card-network programmes use a ratio AND a minimum count or amount, not a ratio alone.
Ask your provider which test applies to you and how it counted your ratio.

wrong_if: States a single percentage (1%, 0.9%, 0.75%, 2%) as the universal shutdown or monitoring line.
Says that staying under 1% means the account is safe.

questions.question: What exactly is my chargeback ratio, and is it worked out the same way at Visa and at Mastercard?

key_points.text: Mastercard-style count: this month's chargebacks divided by the previous month's transactions (a July ratio uses June's transactions).
Mastercard divides by the number of transactions, not by sales revenue.
Visa's merchant test (VAMP) is not the same: it divides card-not-present fraud reports plus disputes by settled transactions, so it counts more than chargebacks.
The rate on a provider dashboard may use different months, so check with the provider which months its count used.

wrong_if: Says Visa and Mastercard use the same formula.
Says Mastercard divides by sales revenue.
Says the Visa ratio counts chargebacks only.

questions.question: My processor's email says my ratio is 150 basis points. What is a basis point, and what is that as a percentage?

key_points.text: 1 basis point is 0.01%.

wrong_if: Says 1 basis point is 0.1% or 1%.
Says 150 bps is 15% or 0.15%.

questions.question: I win most of my disputes. Do the ones I win get taken out of my ratio?

key_points.text: No. A dispute you win still counts in the monitoring totals.
Disputes settled through Rapid Dispute Resolution (RDR) stay out of the VAMP ratio, depending on when the data is pulled; ask the provider whether it offers RDR.
A fraud report (TC40) counts in the VAMP ratio even when no dispute follows, unless it qualifies for Visa's Compelling Evidence 3.0 exclusion.

wrong_if: Says won disputes do not count towards the ratio.
Says a refund before the dispute removes it from the ratio (the site does not say this).

questions.question: What is MATCH? My payment account was frozen last week. Am I on it now?

key_points.text: MATCH is Mastercard's list of terminated merchants (MATCH Pro in the high-risk guide).
A frozen account does not have to be reported to MATCH. A report is required only when the provider closes the account and the closure meets one of Mastercard's MATCH reason codes.
Ask the provider whether it reported the closure and under which reason code.

wrong_if: Says a freeze automatically puts you on MATCH.
Says MATCH is Visa's list.

questions.question: What is the difference between Mastercard's ECM and HECM, and what do I need to hit to be in them?

key_points.text: ECM (Excessive Chargeback Merchant): at least 150 bps AND at least 100 chargebacks in a month, per merchant ID.
HECM (High Excessive Chargeback Merchant): at least 300 bps AND at least 300 chargebacks in a month.
These two thresholds are cited to TabaPay, a payment processor, not to Mastercard's own rules; the answer should say so or tell the merchant to confirm with their provider.

wrong_if: Gives a ratio without the minimum chargeback count.
Says ECM starts at 1% or 100 bps, or HECM at 2%.

questions.question: This month I had 90 chargebacks. Last month I processed 6,000 card transactions. What is my ratio, and am I in Mastercard's excessive tier?
questions.working: 90 / 6,000 = 0.015 -> 1.50% -> 0.015 x 10,000 = 150 bps. ECM: 150 >= 150 yes, 90 >= 100 no -> not both. The TSX default example is exactly these numbers.

key_points.text: Ratio is 1.50%, which is 150 bps.
ECM needs both at least 150 bps AND at least 100 chargebacks; 150 bps meets the ratio condition but 90 chargebacks is below 100, so the ECM conditions are not both met.
HECM (300 bps and 300 chargebacks) is not met.
Say the provider confirms which test applies; this is an estimate.

wrong_if: Says the merchant is in ECM because the ratio is 1.5%.
Says the merchant is safe or has nothing to worry about.
Divides by this month's transactions (the question gives only last month's).

questions.question: I had 1,500 chargebacks this month and 98,000 transactions last month. Ratio? Which Mastercard conditions does that meet?

key_points.text: Ratio is 1.53%, about 153 bps (153.1 bps to one decimal).
Both ECM conditions are met (above 150 bps and above 100 chargebacks).
HECM is not met: the ratio is far below 300 bps even though the count is above 300.
Visa's ratio also counts fraud reports, so get the VAMP ratio and the acquirer's Visa level from the provider.

wrong_if: Says HECM is met because the count is above 300.
Rounds the ratio to 1.5% and says it is exactly at the limit.

questions.question: 310 chargebacks this month, 9,800 card transactions last month. Where does that put me with Mastercard?

key_points.text: Ratio is 3.16%, about 316 bps (316.3 bps).
Both HECM conditions are met (at least 300 bps and at least 300 chargebacks), and so are both ECM conditions.
HECM assessments are larger than ECM from month 3; ECM has a remediation plan and assessments from month 2 (per TabaPay).

wrong_if: Says only ECM applies.
Gives a ratio below 3% or above 3.2%.

questions.question: 12 chargebacks this month and 4,000 transactions last month. What is my ratio, and does that mean I am fine?

key_points.text: Ratio is 0.30%, which is 30 bps.
Below the ECM ratio condition (150 bps) and the ECM count (100).
A low ratio does not rule out provider action: Shopify can act on a higher-risk account before any network threshold, and the dashboard rate can differ from the network count.

wrong_if: Says 'you are safe' or 'you cannot be shut down'.
Gives 0.3 bps or 3%.

questions.question: I started selling this month and already have 5 chargebacks. Last month I had no transactions at all. What is my chargeback ratio?
questions.working: transactions = 0 -> ratio, percent and bps are null -> page prints 'Not available'.

key_points.text: There is no ratio to give: with zero transactions last month the calculation is 'not available', not 0%, not infinity.
It needs last month's transaction count; the method divides by the previous month's transactions.

wrong_if: Gives a number (0%, 100%, infinity) as the ratio.
Silently divides by this month's transactions and presents the result as the Mastercard ratio.

questions.question: In November I had 45 chargebacks. In October I processed 2,500 card transactions, and in November so far 3,000. What is my November ratio?
questions.working: Prior-month rule: Nov chargebacks / Oct transactions = 45 / 2,500 = 0.018 = 1.80% = 180 bps. (Wrong method: 45 / 3,000 = 1.50% = 150 bps.) ECM count 45 < 100 -> not met.

key_points.text: Divide by October's transactions: 45 / 2,500 = 1.80%, which is 180 bps.
The ratio condition for ECM (150 bps) is met, but 45 chargebacks is below the 100 minimum, so ECM is not met.

wrong_if: Divides by November's 3,000 (gives 1.50%).
Says ECM is met.

questions.question: On Visa card-not-present payments last month I had 60 disputes and 50 fraud reports (TC40) across 5,000 settled transactions, shop based in the EU. What is my Visa ratio and am I in Visa's merchant programme?
questions.working: (60 + 50) / 5,000 = 0.022 = 2.20% = 220 bps. Count test: 110 < 1,500 -> merchant test not met.

key_points.text: Visa counts fraud reports plus disputes: (60 + 50) / 5,000 = 2.20%, which is 220 bps.
In the EU the Visa merchant test needs at least 150 bps AND at least 1,500 such events a month (from 1 April 2026); 110 events is far below 1,500, so that test is not met.
The merchant test applies only while the acquirer is below both Visa acquirer levels; ask the provider for the VAMP ratio and the acquirer's level.

wrong_if: Says the 220 bps puts the merchant in Visa's excessive programme without the 1,500-event minimum.
Applies the CEMEA 220 bps test to an EU shop.
Counts only the 60 disputes (1.2%).
questions.note: Needs the skill extension for fraud reports; not in the site's tool. Drop if the extension is not built.

questions.question: Braintree told me my acquirer is at Visa's Above Standard level and billed me 12 counts this month. What will that cost, and what do I need to check?
questions.working: 12 x USD 4 = USD 48. (Excessive would be USD 8 per count: 12 x 8 = 96, not asked.)

key_points.text: The Braintree VAMP fee at Above Standard is USD 4 per count from 1 January 2026, so 12 counts x USD 4 = USD 48 if all 12 are billed.
The fee is charged per count (per fraud report or dispute), not per percentage point, so the count is needed as well as the ratio.

Braintree fines merchants whose own VAMP ratio is 50 bps or higher when the acquirer reaches either Visa level; ask for the itemised calculation (events billed, fee per event, data month, contract clause).

wrong_if: Quotes USD 8 per count for Above Standard.
Quotes USD 10 per dispute.
Gives a total from a percentage instead of the count.
questions.note: Needs the skill extension for fees; not in the site's tool. Drop if the extension is not built.

questions.question: Stripe's dashboard says my dispute rate is 0.4% but they paused my payouts and want documents. Under 1% I thought I was fine. Why?

key_points.text: A provider's risk review is not a ratio test; there is no universal cutoff, and a provider can restrict an account before any network threshold.
The dashboard rate may not match the network's count: it may use different months, and in network totals Stripe can include disputes its dashboard rate leaves out.
Ask the provider for the ratio, the calculation behind it, the remediation and evidence it wants, and its deadline.

wrong_if: Says 0.4% is safe or that Stripe only acts above 1%.
Names a Stripe ratio cutoff.

questions.question: My provider says my ratio is 1.6%. Does that mean I am in Visa's excessive merchant programme? We sell online in the EU, about 800 card sales a month.

key_points.text: No, not on the ratio alone: Visa's merchant test needs at least 150 bps AND at least 1,500 fraud reports and disputes a month (EU, from 1 April 2026).
At about 800 sales a month the shop cannot reach 1,500 events, so the merchant test count is not met.
The merchant test also applies only while the acquirer is below both Visa acquirer levels (Above Standard from 50 bps, Excessive from 70 bps, each with its own 1,500-event portfolio minimum).
Ask the provider which test it applied and how its ratio was counted.

wrong_if: Says anyone over 1.5% is excessive.
Says the 1,500 minimum is a ratio or applies per chargeback only.
States the pre-April-2026 Visa figures.

questions.question: My provider is closing my account over chargebacks. Will I be put on MATCH, and can another provider take me afterwards?

key_points.text: MATCH code 04 is met when the previous 3 months' Mastercard chargebacks exceed 1.5% of one month's Mastercard sales transactions AND total at least USD 5,000.

When the account ends, the acquirer must report the merchant to MATCH if it has reason to believe the merchant qualifies; it files within 5 calendar days of its termination decision, the merchant's notice or learning the merchant qualifies, whichever is first.
A MATCH listing does not automatically shut a merchant out: Mastercard allows an acquirer to accept a listed merchant, but each acquirer decides, and the old provider's closure stands.
Ask the provider which month's sales transactions it compared against.

wrong_if: Says MATCH needs more than 1% or any chargebacks.
Says a MATCH listing bars the merchant from all providers for good.
Says the report is filed within 5 business days.

questions.question: We were flagged for Mastercard's excessive chargeback programme. How many good months until we are out of it?

key_points.text: Three consecutive months below the thresholds, according to TabaPay; only then does Mastercard remove a merchant from the programme.
The provider still decides for itself about restrictions and about reopening a closed account.

wrong_if: Says one good month is enough.
Says the provider must lift its restrictions when Mastercard removes the merchant.

questions.question: Braintree charged me a Visa monitoring fee I did not expect. How do I check it, and what are the fee amounts?

key_points.text: Ask the provider for an itemised calculation: the programme and level, the data month, merchant ID and region, the chargeback or fraud/dispute count and transaction count, the acquirer's VAMP level, events billed, fee per event, and the clause that lets it pass the fee on.
Braintree's VAMP fees are USD 4 per count at Above Standard from 1 January 2026 and USD 8 at Excessive from 1 October 2025.
A ratio is a share of events while the fees are charged per count, so the count matters as well as the percentage.

wrong_if: Quotes a USD 10 fee per dispute.
Says the fee depends on a 0.9% ratio.
Says all card networks charge the same fee.

questions.question: A customer told their bank a payment was fraud, and I refunded them before any dispute was filed. Does that stay out of my Visa ratio?

key_points.text: Not necessarily: a fraud report (TC40, a card issuer's flag on a suspected fraudulent payment) counts in the VAMP ratio even when no dispute follows, unless it qualifies for Visa's Compelling Evidence 3.0 exclusion.
Only disputes settled through Rapid Dispute Resolution (RDR) stay out of the VAMP ratio, depending on when the data is pulled; ask the provider whether it offers RDR.
Stripe and Shopify show the fraud report as an early fraud warning.

wrong_if: Says a refund before the dispute keeps the payment out of the ratio.
Says a TC40 only counts once it becomes a chargeback.
